title: A common data foundation supports fair comparisons
sub: The expanded cohort contains 449,199 snapshots from 25,925 patients.
takeaway: All current model comparisons use the same validation rows. A snapshot is one patient at one date.
note: Patient-separated splits. Current development does not score TEST. Snapshot window: February 2022 to January 2026.

title: Medical histories enrich the original tabular approach
sub: The current phase combines twelve monthly history windows with one AutoML summary anchor.
items: Diagnosis, procedure and prescription activity describe what happened and how frequently.
Monthly text representations of medical codes add information about the types of recorded activity. These are not clinical notes.
Static AutoML features provide context. Sleep-study and sleep-wake timing features test whether recency adds predictive value.
note: A full twelve-anchor historical AutoML panel remains a separate experiment.

title: How repeated medical-code text reaches NLP fusion
sub: The current method turns medical-code descriptions into numbers; it does not read clinical notes.
rows: "sleep study" occurs twice in October and once in September.
Word and two-word phrase counts, weighted by event counts.
For a term count of 2, sublinear TF = 1 + ln(2), approximately 1.69; count 1 becomes 1.
TRAIN-fitted IDF weights, then each monthly text vector is normalised.
Count channel still records 2 studies versus 1 study.
Counts and text features are concatenated for each month.
The sequence model sees the twelve monthly vectors and their positions.
A learned score; repeat codes alone do not prove disease severity or treatment need.
note: Exact final text weights depend on the frozen TRAIN vocabulary and IDF. If a document repeats only the same phrase, normalisation can remove the overall repetition scale; counts retain frequency.

title: NLP fusion leads the current top-10% ranking
sub: 2.954 versus 2.533: +16.6%, or 48 additional positive snapshots at the same 10% capacity.
takeaway: Paired lift interval: +0.009 to +0.802. NLP leads at 10%; static fusion leads slightly at 20% and 30%.
note: Development validation. Added information differs across models. Lift is selected positive rate divided by overall positive rate.

title: What does this mean for our teams?
sub: A better shortlist could make the same review effort more productive.
items: Among 6,797 selected patient-date records, NLP fusion captured 337 positive records versus 289 for the static development control.
Refresh the priority list with monthly histories, then apply agreed patient deduplication and HCP mapping before routing it for review.
More unique relevant patients at the same capacity, acceptable run cost and reliable delivery. Outreach response and treatment benefit are not yet measured.
note: 48 additional positive snapshots are not 48 additional people. Positive means the recorded target event occurred in the outcome window.

title: Timing features improved their matched control
sub: Both arms use 1,000 trees without early stopping. Timing added 44 positive snapshots: 235 to 279.
takeaway: The timing arm still trails the earlier early-stopped static control: 279 versus 289 captures. Tune them under one protocol next.
note: Paired lift difference +0.386; 95% interval [+0.098, +0.689]. Gain versus the stronger early-stopped baseline is untested.

title: Repeated runs show a consistent lead for NLP fusion
sub: Each model was trained three times with different random starting points.
takeaway: Selected-model lift drops by 7 to 11% from training to validation. Repeated-run consistency does not prove performance on new populations.
note: Values are validation Lift@10%. Gaps use training lift as the denominator. Validation was used to select checkpoints.

note: Both paths are proposals. Native support in the current AutoML platform has not been established. A trained fusion model is not itself a raw feature.

title: A fair production comparison needs one agreed test
sub: Verification proposal: obtain provenance and score coverage before running or claiming a result.
rows: Same target window, eligibility, snapshot cutoff, ranking unit and capacity.
Written comparison specification and locked evaluation keys.
Frozen model version, training dates/patients, feature vintage and tuning history.
Evidence that the evaluation is independent, or an explicit limitation.
Exact patient-date scores from both models; complete outcome follow-up.
Coverage report; no nearest-date or selective-overlap substitution.
Lift and captures at 10/20/30%; paired patient intervals; unique patients and runtime.
A release decision using thresholds agreed before seeing results.
note: Production remains unchanged. Access to frozen scores and training provenance, and agreement on a fresh evaluation population, are prerequisites.
